results.title: Don't say hop before you jump
results.original_title: Don't say hop before you jump
results.overview: Director Nikita Lukyanov collaborates with creative director Can Dağarslanı for the short film Don’t Say Hop Before You Jump – featuring equestrian vaulting sisters Alice & Helen Layher. Shot on 16mm film,the visual short follows the German sisters when their daily equestrian vaulting rituals slip into the surreal. As their horse circles the arena anticlockwise, time begins to rewind, carrying the sisters back to the childhood where their shared rhythm began.

In the city, João encounters paranoia and insomnia; amidst the chaos, he meets someone who tries to convince him to return the stone and reconcile with his people.

results.title: The New Library – Part one | 1983 - 2026
results.overview: As Rotterdam’s Central Library enters a new chapter, The New Library – Part One documents a defining moment in the life of one of the city’s most recognisable public buildings. Following the careful dismantling of its distinctive interior, the film traces the library’s origins and explores how it has embodied changing ideas about knowledge, public space, and urban life over the past forty years. Combining archival material with contemporary voices, it places the building within Rotterdam’s continuous process of reinvention, asking how a city can move forward while remaining connected to the places that shape its collective memory. The first chapter of a documentary diptych, the film offers a timely portrait of an iconic Post ’65 landmark and the questions its future raises for the city and its inhabitants.

results.title: A Place in the Middle
results.overview: From aerobics to performance art, what really goes on inside Amsterdam’s deconsecrated churches? As the number of so-called third places where people can gather continues to shrink, perhaps churches could once again fulfil that role. These former sacred spaces still bear traces of their original purpose. How does the history of these buildings shape the activities that take place there today?

results.title: Such a Thing Like Happiness
results.overview: Herman Hertzberger’s LiMa Wohnhof was conceived as an experiment in social housing that combined structuralist principles, participatory design and collective self-building. Four decades later, this film explores how architecture can evolve and adapt in order to allow each generation to redefine what it means to live together.
